### Invoking a Server Action with the form action attribute

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/02-guides/forms.mdx

Server Actions passed to a form's action attribute automatically receive a FormData object to extract input values. Always verify authentication and authorization inside the action before mutating data or revalidating the cache.

```tsx
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'

export default function Page() {
  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {
    'use server'

    const session = await auth()
    if (!session?.user) {
      throw new Error('Unauthorized')
    }

    const rawFormData = {
      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),
      amount: formData.get('amount'),
      status: formData.get('status'),
    }

    // mutate data
    // revalidate the cache
  }

  return <form action={createInvoice}>...</form>
}
```

```jsx
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'

export default function Page() {
  async function createInvoice(formData) {
    'use server'

    const session = await auth()
    if (!session?.user) {
      throw new Error('Unauthorized')
    }

    const rawFormData = {
      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),
      amount: formData.get('amount'),
      status: formData.get('status'),
    }

    // mutate data
    // revalidate the cache
  }

  return <form action={createInvoice}>...</form>
}
```

--------------------------------

### Invoke a Server Function with a Form Action in TypeScript

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/07-mutating-data.mdx

Demonstrates invoking a Server Function via a form's action prop and extracting submitted fields from FormData in TypeScript.

```tsx
import { createPost } from '@/app/actions'

export function Form() {
  return (
    <form action={createPost}>
      <input type="text" name="title" />
      <input type="text" name="content" />
      <button type="submit">Create</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

```ts
'use server'

import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'

export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session?.user) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
  }

  const title = formData.get('title')
  const content = formData.get('content')

  // Mutate data
  // Revalidate cache
}
```

--------------------------------

### Performing mutations with Server Actions using next/form

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/02-components/form.mdx

Pass a Server Action function directly to the action prop of next/form to handle form submissions and mutations.

```tsx
import Form from 'next/form'
import { createPost } from '@/posts/actions'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Form action={createPost}>
      <input name="title" />
      {/* ... */}
      <button type="submit">Create Post</button>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

```jsx
import Form from 'next/form'
import { createPost } from '@/posts/actions'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Form action={createPost}>
      <input name="title" />
      {/* ... */}
      <button type="submit">Create Post</button>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

```js
  // Revalidate cache
}
```

### How to create forms with Server Actions > How it works

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/02-guides/forms.mdx

React extends the HTML [`<form>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [`action`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.

When used in a form, the function automatically receives the [`FormData`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [`FormData` methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):

> **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [`Object.fromEntries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: `const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)`. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with `$ACTION_`.
